drills.q: You try to relabel an existing Deployment's selector via kubectl apply and it fails. Why, and what are your two options?
drills.a: selector.matchLabels is immutable after creation, API validation rejects the change. Options: delete and recreate the Deployment (loses ReplicaSet/rollout history), or never touch it — get the selector correct on first creation.

drills.q: You scale a StatefulSet from 5 to 2 replicas expecting the freed storage to be reclaimed automatically, but kubectl get pvc still shows 5 PVCs. Bug or expected?
drills.a: Expected. persistentVolumeClaimRetentionPolicy defaults whenScaled and whenDeleted to Retain — a deliberate data-safety default so a routine scale-down can't silently destroy data. Set whenScaled: Delete explicitly if the workload doesn't need that data to persist.

drills.q: A CronJob meant to run every 5 minutes is producing duplicate database writes. Diagnose.
drills.a: concurrencyPolicy is at its default, Allow — if a run takes longer than 5 minutes, the next scheduled run starts anyway, overlapping with the still-running one and both writing concurrently. Fix: set concurrencyPolicy: Forbid (skip if still running) or Replace (kill and restart), depending on the desired semantics.

drills.q: A Job manifest sets restartPolicy: Always on its pod template. What happens when you apply it?
drills.a: The API server rejects it at validation time — Always is incompatible with a Job ever reaching a terminal completed state, since it means 'restart no matter what.' Must be OnFailure or Never.

drills.q: Your log-shipper DaemonSet isn't running on your GPU node pool, which is exactly where you need the logs most. What do you check?
drills.a: The GPU nodes' taints (kubectl describe node | grep Taints) against the DaemonSet pod template's tolerations. GPU pools are commonly tainted to keep non-GPU workloads off; DaemonSet still respects taints like any pod, it doesn't bypass them, so a missing toleration silently excludes it.

drills.q: A CronJob 'just stopped running' after a multi-hour control-plane outage, with no error visible in the CronJob's own YAML. What's the mechanism, and how do you confirm and fix it?
drills.a: If the controller detects >=100 missed schedule times since it last checked, it stops scheduling that CronJob entirely rather than firing 100+ overlapping catch-up Jobs. Confirm via controller-manager logs for a 'too many missed start times' message. Not fixable via a CronJob field (startingDeadlineSeconds is a different, per-run knob) — requires manual Job trigger and investigating the outage cause.

drills.q: A rolling Deployment update appears stuck at '1 of 3 updated' for several minutes but hasn't errored. What's happening and what do you check first?
drills.a: The new ReplicaSet's pods are likely failing their readiness probe, so the rollout can't progress past maxUnavailable bounds; it won't be marked Failed until progressDeadlineSeconds (default 600s) elapses with no progress. Check kubectl describe pod on the new pods for readiness probe failures rather than waiting out the deadline.

drills.q: Why would a team deliberately choose StatefulSet updateStrategy: OnDelete instead of the default RollingUpdate for a production database cluster?
drills.a: RollingUpdate's guarantee (reverse-ordinal order, wait for Ready) doesn't account for domain-specific safety conditions like replication lag or leader status. OnDelete hands control to an external operator that decides exactly when each replica is safe to bounce based on that domain knowledge, rather than trusting StatefulSet's generic ordering.

drills.q: A Job has completions: 10, parallelism: 3, and non-indexed completion mode. How do the pods know which piece of work to do?
drills.a: They don't, inherently — non-indexed Jobs give no per-pod differentiation, so the application itself must pull work from an external queue (each of up to 3 concurrent pods grabs the next item until 10 succeed). If pods need a static, deterministic slice of work instead, use completionMode: Indexed, which injects JOB_COMPLETION_INDEX (0..completions-1) into each pod.
